title: Winter Fright Night
subtitle: Put it out—put out the lights!

items.text: Conductress's Cabin

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: No. I'm not going with you! NEVER!
Little William clings to the seat rail, screaming loud enough to pierce steel.
After the quarantine order, passengers are scattered, some herded into the conductress's cabin.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Let go.
Soldiers pry open the boy's stubborn fingers one by one.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Officers, with all due respect, you've taken a dozen passengers already.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: May I ask where you're taking them?

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Shh!
A rifle raises, muzzle aimed at the boot now wedged in the doorframe.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Step back, ma'am.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Nobody leaves the carriage until quarantine is over.
She says nothing but pulls her foot back.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier I
items.text: Just work with us, please, and soon this'll all be over.
The soldier slings the boy under his arm and marches off.

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: Annabelle! No!
The heavy lock clicks shut, leaving only anxious passengers and stone-faced soldiers.

items.speaker: Passenger II
items.text: No food, no water, and no idea how long they'll keep us. This isn't separation. It's imprisonment!

items.speaker: Passenger III
items.text: Worse than that! At least prisoners know their sentence!

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: They took William and Ms. Dorothy, and Rubuska hasn't come back, either.
Sensing the soldier's warning glare, the girl clutches her doll tight.
She presses her communicator and is met with static.
Her words and any vital intelligence she could share are stranded with her.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Something's jamming my signal. And the teleport disk isn't working either. Heh, someone came prepared.
Semmelweis approaches the door and peers through the window into the next car.
The scene is carnage.
The once opulent carriage is a spectacle of disaster, its walls painted with blood.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: What on earth ...?
Aaahahah!
A low, drawn-out wail comes from the corner.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Hm? Seems a little early for that soldier to be back.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier II
items.text: What the—Everything alright?

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier II
items.text: Ah. Idiot. Better go check on him.
The soldier stiffens, lifts his rifle, and hurries away.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: He's gone. Conductress, I think it's time you and I had a heart-to-heart.
She steps up to the conductress, blunt and direct.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: This is all wrong.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: No food, no water, no radio signal. I don't believe they're doing anything to protect the passengers from infection. This isn't a quarantine; this is a cover-up.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: What are you suggesting?
The investigator reveals the badge in her hand.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: This insignia. I believe you have one just like it.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: That's what you were sniffing around for.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: It belongs to an organization I've been tracking—Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Manus Vindictae?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: At first, I thought you were one of them. Yet here you are, locked up like the rest of us. Perhaps Pyrrhos doesn't trust you all that much.
Corvus's look of confusion—certainly genuine—serves to confirm her suspicion.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: The Manus are a group of extremist arcanists that take pleasure in chaos and despair. Heartless bastards, every last one of them.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Never heard of them. The badge is Pyrrhos's, some kind of identifier for his men.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: When I took this mission, our intelligence suggested that the vampire I'm after may be associated with Manus Vindictae. If Pyrrhos is working with them, he could be working with the vampire aboard.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: It's possible, indeed, that he could be the vampire himself.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Pyrrhos is a vampire.
No more evasions and equivocal answers, the conductress calmly reveals the truth.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: We were comrades-in-arms once. One of the most capable fighters we had—clever, composed, he always made the right decisions when it counted.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I would never have thought he'd be involved with such an organization.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'm afraid it's almost certain that he's the vampire Manus Vindictae had sent to this train.
At last, a lead. Semmelweis breathes a long, drawn-out breath, letting the weight fall off her shoulders.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Now that things are out in the open, do you have any idea what happened to my squad?
The reply comes with a resigned shake of her head.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: No. I haven't seen any of them.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I'd know. As I've said before, this isn't the first time we've had the Foundation aboard. Last time there was a confrontation between them and some other arcanists.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Hah. Sometimes, I think causing trouble might be our primary mission.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: But let's return to our vampire. I'm still not certain what Manus Vindictae is up to, but ...

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: That vampire infection couldn't have been a coincidence. Someone meant for it to happen.
The conductress sneers, her fingers tracing the silver engraving on her pistol.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I've known Pyrrhos a long time. But lately he's been strange. I usually wouldn't attempt to interfere with his business.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: But these are my passengers—my train.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Glad to see we're finally on the same page. So, Conductress, can you get us out of here?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Haste makes waste, Investigator. There's a loose thread I'm waiting for, then we can pull all of this together.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: We're long past the point for patience, if you ask me.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Ah!
A bloody hand slaps the window, smearing crimson streaks down the glass.
Oh ...

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Another Infected!

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: What was that about "haste makes waste," Conductress?

items.speaker: Infected Passenger
items.text: Through. Let me through.
Thud. Thud.
The man mumbles flatly, headbutting the glass again and again until blood pours from his brow.

items.speaker: Infected Passenger
items.text: Let me through.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Ah!

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: He's ... He's breaking in.

items.speaker: Infected Passenger
items.text: Let me through, let me through, let me through, let me through.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Conductress, there must be something muting arcane skills on this train.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Arcane skills aren't everything.
She pulls the passengers behind her, draws her sidearm, and takes aim.

items.speaker: Infected Passenger
items.text: Uggh!
Before the shot fires, the infected passenger is yanked away by an unseen force.
Another splash of blood smears across the window.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: What was that? Another Infected?
The sound dies. Then comes a faint rustling outside the door.
A familiar face rises into view beyond the glass.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: No. It's just me.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Is she what you were waiting for, Conductress?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Exactly. Aima, you drew that soldier away, yes?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Mm-hm. I waited for just the right moment.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Well done. What's our situation?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: There are Infected everywhere—the cabins, the hallways—all through the train. They seem to be running out from the station warehouse.
The stewardess goes pale, recounting everything she saw outside.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: There's blood everywhere, too, on the walls, on the floor ... I tried my best not to look at it.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Was it you who killed that Infected just now?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Well …
She tugs shyly at her eyepatch.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I ensure all crew on the "Danube Dawn" are trained in self-defense. It's hardly surprising.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Go ahead, Aima.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Oh, yes.
She lowers her head, clenched fist trembling.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: I saw those soldiers in their carriages. I thought they'd be caring for the passengers or removing the Infected, but ...

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: They did nothing, as if it were of no concern to them whatsoever.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: They took the passengers, one by one, to some kind of detention room for inspection, then sent them to the warehouse. But then they started coming back out, like that.
She wipes a smear of blood from her cheek, then slips her finger briefly into her mouth.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Uncle Pyrrhos ... I don't know what's happened to him, but we have to find him.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I see. How many soldiers remain aboard the train?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Not many. A few were sent to guard the detention room. I-I think we can handle the ones that are left!
The meek girl pumps her fist in an uncommon gesture of confidence.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Good. Everything is in place; let's move.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Wait, shh. I hear footsteps.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: They saw me just then. I can't be seen here again.
Aima's eye darts around before she ducks behind the curtains.
Then, the door is opened forcefully.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier II
items.text: Damn it. This is getting out of hand.
Soldiers, having dealt with the "unexpected occurrence," rush in, weapons raised at the frightened passengers.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier II
items.text: Where were we? On to the next passenger.
The muzzle drifts left and right, finally settling on Annabelle.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier II
items.text: You. Little girl. It's your turn.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Me? I don't want to go!

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier II
items.text: Come now, be quiet.
The muzzle is locked in place.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You heard her.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: She said: No.
In the scuffle, two shots ring out, each slamming into the metal ceiling.
The soldier tries to wrench back his rifle, but Corvus's grip is unyielding.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier II
items.text: You! Let go!

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: She's not going.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier III
items.text: What's going on? Stand down, all of you!
Another soldier appears behind them, gun in one hand, whistle in the other, his fingers shaking.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Go, Aima.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Y-Yes. Understood!
The stewardess tears off her eyepatch, revealing her other blood-red eye.
Before the whistle meets his lips, she leaps from the shadows, slamming into him.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier III
items.text: Aargh! Get off me!
In a second, her arm snakes around his neck.

items.speaker: Border Checkpoint Soldier III
items.text: Uggh!

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Apologies for the shock, but thank you for the gun and whistle.
The soldiers collapse.
Aima drags them to the corner, exhales, and pulls her eyepatch down.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: No one will take you away, Annabelle, at least for the time being.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Hm? Why is everyone so quiet?
Passengers stare in slack-jawed silence. The girl runs up, tugging excitedly at her skirt.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Red eyes, fangs ... A-Are you a vampire too, Stewardess?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Oh. Well, yes, I am. But don't worry. It won't affect your service in any way whatsoever!

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: But your other eye is all clear and blue, like a lake, not red at all. How did you do that?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: I-I'm not a pure-blood vampire.
She shakes her head quietly before looking away; she has no intention of going any deeper into the subject.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I have to say, I didn't expect the stories of a vampire train to actually hold any truth. Though I doubt any of the stories had our vampires pouring tea and fluffing pillows.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: There was never any truth to them. Aima may be a vampire, yes, but she's never done anyone harm.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Then, earlier, in the forest ...
She recalls the night in the snow, with the two of them pressed close together.
The storm was so thick she could barely see, only mist, trees, and a red scarf whipping in the wind.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: It was bloodthirst, so I gave her mine. It's an arrangement of ours.
Corvus adjusts the scarf around the small stewardess's neck.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: First a secret carriage, now a vampire stewardess. What else might you be hiding up your sleeve?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Nothing of your concern. We share a common interest, so let us treat each other as comrades.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: There may be tricks up my sleeve, but for now, we watch, wait, and then strike.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: You surprise me more and more, Conductress. Comrades it is, but what's our next move?

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: I wish there were some other way, old friend.
She exhales, a cold light flashing in her eyes.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Aima, how many passengers are left on board?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: I didn't count precisely; there were already quite a few that were taken to the detention room.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Oh! Conductress, are you going to ...
Corvus pushes through the crowd to a tall cabinet and yanks it open.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You there. Ever handled a gun before?

items.speaker: Stowaways
items.text: Whoa ...
Weapons line the wall in neat rows, gleaming under the light.
Each one meticulously polished and ready, as if awaiting their call to battle.

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Yet another surprise. I don't think I ever would have expected you to be lugging an armory around with you.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: It's a hobby. Take this.
She takes a pistol down and tosses it to Semmelweis.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Silver bullets are more effective than arcane skill when dealing with vampires and their Infected.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Anyone old enough to handle a weapon, arm yourselves. We have a fierce battle ahead.
